title: Private upgrade step-lattice and retention-compat migration orchestrator
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Build an orchestrator and toolkit for performing coordinated upgrades of Redwood Private clusters (VPC/on-prem) that: 1) applies manifest-driven, step-lattice upgrades across heterogeneous node pools and state shards; 2) supports transactional schema migrations, state retention compatibility, and incremental compaction; 3) exposes fine-grained rollout gates (metrics, telemetry, manual hold) and automated rollback on invariants. The goal is zero or minimal downtime upgrades for customers on LTS channels and to provide safe dry-run / staged rollouts for enterprise installs.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can compute an upgrade plan (manifest -> step-lattice graph) for a Private cluster with multiple node pools and persistent stores
Plan execution supports explicit quiesce, apply-migration, reconcile, and resume phases with idempotent operations
Automated preflight probes validate compatibility for 95% of clusters in staging (schema checksum, KV snapshot validation, disk layout compatibility)
Canary rollout flows can progressively upgrade 5%, 25%, then 100% of nodes with gate checks on latency, error-rate, and custom customer probes
Rollback path proven in integration tests: operator reverts to previous runtime and replays state translator to restore pre-upgrade invariants
Operator exposes audit logs, change-ids, and per-cluster dry-run reports suitable for customer review
Tooling is documented and gated by a security review (KMS/HSM integration for private key material).
background: Existing private upgrade tooling is ad-hoc: a set of scripts and manual runbooks. Prior ENG work (see dependencies) built migration primitives and dry-run harnesses but lacks a unified orchestrator for multi-shard transactional migrations and retention compatibility verification. Customers on LTS channels require predictable upgrade windows and rollback guarantees; platform teams need first-class rollout gates and telemetry integration for SLO safety.
proposed_solution:
Introduce a manifest-driven orchestration layer (upgrade-api) that translates release manifests into a directed acyclic step-lattice. Each step is annotated with intent (schema-migrate, binary-rollout, cache-invalidate, retention-trim), pre/post probes, and compensating actions. Key pieces:
- Planner: computes safe batches based on topology, shard affinity, and canary budget.
- Executor: idempotent step runner with transactional hooks for stateful operations.
- Translator: small library to convert on-disk and KV formats for compatibility (runs as a pre-migrate dry-run and as part of controlled migration steps).
- Gate engine: supports metric-based, time-based, and manual hold gates with integration to Console alerting and tracing.
- Audit & telemetry: immutable logs for each step, plus per-stage snapshots and post-upgrade validation reports.
We will reuse kernel selection and runtime-level rollout primitives where possible and extend the existing agent to accept plans and report progress via the control plane.

rollout_plan: Phase A: internal dogfood on non-production clusters using dry-run mode; gather compatibility failures and refine translator rules
Phase B: staged canary on 2 pilot customers (opt-in) with 5% -> 25% -> 100% bump; manual hold gates enabled by default
Phase C: broader rollout to enterprise customers on private dedicated (rolling windows) with optional migration-as-a-service support
Phase D: full LTS channel rollout after two successful customer migrations and green signals from analytics
monitoring_and_rollback: Expose per-step metrics: duration, success/failure, pre/post-probe deltas, and KV diff sizes
Integrate with Console to create temporary SLO dashboards during upgrades; automatic traffic shaping on latency regressions

Rollback strategy: for data-only migrations use compensating translators; for incompatible binary/runtime changes, a coordinated rollback replaces binaries and replays state forwards/backwards depending on migration type
Emergency abort: operator marks cluster 'upgrade-failed' and triggers a fast-path rollback playbook; page on-call and create incident with pre-populated diagnostics bundle
test_plan: Unit tests for planner edge cases (circular deps, conflicting retention policies)
Integration tests: multi-shard cluster upgrade simulations with synthetic workloads (latency and error profiles)
Chaos tests: node flaps, disk pressure, and delayed network to validate idempotency and reconcile
Customer-mirroring test: replay a real customer's snapshot in staging and run dry-run to detect translator gaps
Security tests: ensure key material never leaves customer VPC; run KMS integration tests and static analysis
risks: State translator complexity: unanticipated on-disk layouts from legacy clusters may require custom translators per major version
Long-running migrations may violate customer maintenance windows if not properly budgeted
Rollback safety: certain destructive compactions cannot be trivially reversed; need conservative guards
Operational complexity: adding a powerful orchestrator increases Blast radius if misconfigured
Dependency on agent/connector versions in Private installs could block plan execution
